item.title: 🐚 Weekly Summary — Shell Programming in UNIX
item.description:
This week I completed Lab #12 — Advanced Shell Programming in UNIX. The work focused on writing complex bash scripts using logical control structures and loops.

Table of Contents
  • Goal
  • Task 1: Semaphore Mechanism
  • Task 2: Custom man Command
  • Task 3: Random Letter Generator
  • Conclusions

Goal

Study the basics of programming in the UNIX shell. Learn to write more complex shell scripts using logical control constructs and loops.

Task 1: Semaphore Mechanism

I wrote a shell script implementing a simplified semaphore mechanism. The script:

  • waits up to time t1 for a resource to become free, printing status messages throughout
  • once the resource is free, uses it for time t2 ≠ t1, also printing that the resource is in use

The script was launched in one virtual terminal in the background with output redirected to another terminal (> /dev/tty#). The same script was run in the second terminal in normal mode. This demonstrated how two processes compete for the same shared resource.

The program was then extended to support interaction of three or more concurrent processes through a single semaphore.

Task 2: Custom man Command

I implemented the man command as a shell script. The script:

  • accepts a command name as a command-line argument
  • searches /usr/share/man/man1/ for the corresponding archive
  • if found, displays the help page using less
  • if not found, outputs a message indicating missing documentation

Task 3: Random Letter Generator

Using the built-in $RANDOM variable (which produces pseudo-random numbers in the range 0–32767), I wrote a script that generates a random sequence of Latin alphabet letters. The letter was computed as:

code=$(( RANDOM % 26 + 65 ))
letter=$(printf "\\$(printf '%03o' $code)")

Conclusions

Through this lab I gained practical experience with:

  • process synchronization using file-based semaphores
  • working with the /usr/share/man/ directory structure and documentation format
  • arithmetic operations and the $RANDOM variable in bash
  • redirecting I/O between terminals

Shell scripting is a powerful tool for system-level automation that is difficult to replace with higher-level languages in certain scenarios.

item.title: 🎉 Git Version Control Basics
item.description:
Hello 👋

Table of Contents
  • Introduction
  • Why Git?
  • Core Git Commands
  • How It Works
  • Advantages of Git
  • Conclusion

Introduction

Git is a version control system that allows you to track changes in your code and manage the history of a project. It is widely used in software development and is the industry standard.

Why Git?

Git solves several important problems:

  • stores the full history of project changes
  • allows you to roll back to previous versions
  • enables collaborative work on code
  • provides control and safety for changes

This is especially important when working in a team where multiple people are simultaneously modifying the same project.

Core Git Commands

The most commonly used commands:

  • git init — initialize a repository
  • git add . — stage files
  • git commit -m "message" — save changes
  • git push — push changes to a remote repository
  • git pull — pull changes from remote

How It Works

Git operates through a system of commits. Each commit is a saved state of the project at a specific point in time.

The main workflow:

  1. Modify files
  2. Stage changes (git add)
  3. Create a commit (git commit)
  4. Push to the server (git push)

Advantages of Git

  • high performance
  • distributed system — every developer has a full copy of the project
  • flexibility and reliability
  • wide adoption

Conclusion

Git is an essential tool for any developer. Even a basic understanding of its principles greatly simplifies working with projects and enables effective code management.

item.title: 📚 Bibliography in Academic Writing
item.description:
A bibliography is more than just a list of sources at the end of a paper. It is a tool that demonstrates how deeply an author engaged with the topic and allows readers to verify the information independently.

What Is a Bibliography and Why Does It Matter?

A bibliography is an ordered list of all sources used when writing a scientific or academic paper. It serves several functions:

  • Confirms credibility — readers can verify every claim
  • Protects against plagiarism — all borrowings are explicitly listed
  • Shows research depth — demonstrates the volume of material the author worked through
  • Helps other researchers — find related sources on the topic

Main Citation Styles

Academic practice has several bibliography formatting standards. The choice depends on the discipline and institutional requirements.

GOST R 7.0.5-2008

The Russian national standard, mandatory at most Russian universities. Example for a book:

Ivanov, A. V. Foundations of Scientific Research / A. V. Ivanov. — Moscow : Nauka, 2020. — 320 p.

APA (American Psychological Association)

Used in psychology, sociology, and education:

Ivanov, A. V. (2020). Foundations of scientific research. Nauka.

MLA (Modern Language Association)

Popular in the humanities:

Ivanov, Alexei V. Foundations of Scientific Research. Nauka, 2020.

Types of Sources and Their Formatting

Note

Different source types are formatted differently. It’s important not to mix up the scheme for a book, an article, and a web resource.

Book (monograph): Author, initials. Title. — City : Publisher, year. — Number of pages.

Journal article: Author, initials. Article title // Journal Name. — year. — Vol., No. — pp. pages.

Web resource: Author. Material title [Electronic resource]. — URL: address (accessed: dd.mm.yyyy).

Reference Management Tools

Working with a large number of sources manually is inconvenient. There are dedicated reference manager programs:

Tool Free Notes
Zotero ✅ Best choice for most tasks, browser plugin
Mendeley ✅ Great for PDFs and collaborative work
EndNote ❌ Professional tool for serious researchers
CiteMachine ✅ Online citation generator, quick and simple

Common Mistakes

Warning

These errors appear in most student papers — better to check in advance.

  1. Source is in the text but not in the list — or vice versa
  2. Inconsistent style — some sources in GOST, some in APA
  3. No access date for web resources
  4. Wrong order — GOST requires alphabetical order
  5. Outdated sources without justification — prefer publications from the last 5–10 years

Summary

A well-formatted bibliography is a sign of respect for the reader and for scholarship. Take a little time to learn the required standard, use reference managers, and check your list before submission.
